summary: Revolutionary captain, Provincial Congress delegate and county judge, husband of the Culper spy Anna Strong; John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed.
bio:
Selah Strong (1737–1815) was a delegate to the Provincial Congress and a captain in the Revolution, during which he was held on a British prison ship; after the war he served as a county judge. A 1792 engraving by Cornelius Tiebout shows "the seat of the Hon. Selah Strong, Esqr., St. George's Manor". His wife, Anna Smith Strong, is remembered as the Culper spy; she belonged to a different Smith family and is not a blood relative of John's.

Selah was the son of Thomas Strong and Susannah Thompson, a granddaughter of John Thompson, which makes him John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed on the Thompson side. He was also a great-great-grandson of Bull Smith, and he is related to John more distantly through the Topping family and, if that line holds, through the Brewsters.

military.note: Held on a British prison ship.

researchNotes:
Path: John Thompson → Samuel → Susannah (m. Thomas Strong) → Selah. A great-great-grandson of Bull Smith. Delegate to the Provincial Congress, Revolutionary captain, later county judge; held on a British prison ship. His wife Anna Smith Strong is NOT a blood relative (different Smith family). A Selah Strong of Orange County was executor for James Tuthill Jr. (1756) and witness for Daniel Tuthill (1761) — possibly a namesake relative (not established).

Path verified (Thompson [R4-S1]): John Thompson -> Samuel (1668-1749) -> Susannah (1712-88, m. 1734 Thomas Strong) -> Selah: 2nd cousin 9 times removed. A 1792 engraving by Cornelius Tiebout shows 'the seat of the Hon. Selah Strong, Esqr., St. George's Manor' ([R4-S2]).
